lessons.title: The Power of Prayer
introduction: Prayer is the believer's lifeline to God. Jesus taught that men ought always to pray and not to faint (Luke 18:1). In this lesson we look at why prayer matters, how to pray, and what hinders our prayers.

sections.heading: Why we must pray
points: God commands it: we are told to pray always with all prayer and supplication (Ephesians 6:18).
Prayer brings God's peace that passes understanding (Philippians 4:6-7).
Jesus Himself set the example by praying early and alone (Mark 1:35; Luke 5:16).

sections.heading: How to pray effectively
points: Pray in faith, believing that you receive (Mark 11:24; James 1:6-7).
Pray according to His will (1 John 5:14-15).
Persevere like the widow before the unjust judge (Luke 18:3-5).

sections.heading: Hindrances to prayer
points: Unconfessed sin separates us from God (Isaiah 59:1-2; Psalm 66:18).
Unforgiveness blocks answered prayer (Mark 11:25-26).
Wrong motives: asking amiss to spend it on our lusts (James 4:3).

conclusion: The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much (James 5:16). Make prayer a daily habit, not an emergency exit.
questions: What does Luke 18:1 teach about persistence in prayer?
Name three hindrances to answered prayer from this lesson.
How can you build a consistent prayer life this week?
lessons.prayer: Lord, teach me to pray without ceasing and to trust You for every answer.
lessons.assignment: Keep a prayer journal for seven days. Read Daniel 6:10 and note Daniel's habit.

lessons.title: Living Sacrifices

memory_verse.text: I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that ye present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service.

introduction: After eleven chapters on what God has done for us, Paul turns to how we should live in response. Romans 12:1-2 calls every believer to total surrender and a renewed mind.

sections.heading: Total surrender
body: Under the Old Testament, sacrifices were slain (Leviticus 1:3-9). God now asks for living sacrifices: our whole lives offered daily.
points: Surrender is a response to mercy, not a way to earn it (Romans 12:1; Ephesians 2:8-10).
Our bodies are the temple of the Holy Spirit (1 Corinthians 6:19-20).
Surrender is daily: take up your cross daily (Luke 9:23).

sections.heading: A renewed mind
points: Do not be conformed to this world (Romans 12:2; 1 John 2:15-17).
Renewal comes through the Word (Psalm 119:9-11; John 17:17).
Think on whatever things are true, honest and pure (Philippians 4:8).

sections.heading: Serving with our gifts
points: Think soberly about yourself (Romans 12:3).
One body, many members (Romans 12:4-5; 1 Corinthians 12:12-27).
Use your gift faithfully: prophecy, ministry, teaching, exhorting, giving, leading, mercy (Romans 12:6-8; 1 Peter 4:10).

conclusion: A surrendered life is a transformed life. Present yourself to God afresh this week and look for one way to serve the body of Christ.
questions: What is the difference between Old Testament sacrifices and a living sacrifice?
According to Romans 12:2, how is the mind renewed?
Which of the gifts in Romans 12:6-8 do you see in your life?
lessons.prayer: Father, I present my body to You as a living sacrifice. Renew my mind by Your Word.
lessons.assignment: Memorise Romans 12:1-2 and read 1 Corinthians 12 in full.

lessons.title: Faith That Works

memory_verse.text: Even so faith, if it hath not works, is dead, being alone.

introduction: James challenges a faith that only talks. True saving faith (Ephesians 2:8-9) always shows itself in a changed life (James 2:18).

sections.heading: Faith without works
points: Words without deeds help no one (James 2:15-16; 1 John 3:17-18).
Even the devils believe and tremble (James 2:19).

sections.heading: Examples of living faith
points: Abraham offered Isaac (James 2:21-23; Genesis 22:1-12; Hebrews 11:17-19).
Rahab hid the messengers (James 2:25; Joshua 2:1-21).

conclusion: We are saved by faith alone, but saving faith is never alone. Let your light so shine (Matthew 5:16).
questions: How do Ephesians 2:8-10 and James 2:17 agree?
What did Abraham's obedience reveal about his faith?
lessons.prayer: Lord, let my faith be seen in my works of love.
lessons.assignment: Do one practical act of kindness for someone in need this week.

lessons.title: The Fruit of the Spirit

memory_verse.text: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, meekness, temperance: against such there is no law.

introduction: The Christian life is a contest between the flesh and the Spirit (Galatians 5:17). Victory comes by walking in the Spirit.

sections.heading: Works of the flesh
points: The works of the flesh are manifest (Galatians 5:19-21).
The carnal mind is enmity against God (Romans 8:6-8).

sections.heading: The fruit of the Spirit
points: Fruit grows by abiding in Christ (John 15:4-5).
Love is the first and greatest (1 Corinthians 13:4-7; 1 John 4:7-8).
Walk in the Spirit (Galatians 5:16, 25).

conclusion: Fruit is not manufactured; it grows. Abide in Christ and the fruit will follow.
questions: List the nine qualities of the fruit of the Spirit.
What does John 15:5 teach about fruitfulness?
lessons.prayer: Holy Spirit, produce Your fruit in my life.
lessons.assignment: Choose one quality of the fruit of the Spirit to focus on each day this week.
